content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation source ledger against the disclosure (the conversation file is a truncated duplicate of it and adds nothing).

input.summary: Full preflight completed. I traced every limitation of all 22 claims (apparatus claims 1-12, independent apparatus claim 13 and its dependents 14-17, and method claim 18 with dependents 19-22), every entry in draft/numerals.md (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94), every numbered part and relationship in the Field, Summary, Brief Description of Drawings, Detailed Description and Abstract, and every sentence of the FIG. 1 through FIG. 7 briefs, back to affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md (input/conversation.md is a truncated duplicate of the same USER text and supplies no additional matter; input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority, no-government-support, and the preserved terminology list). The core apparatus and method matter is well supported: rail with flat lower face, upper face, straight longitudinal slot through the rail and printed distance marks beside the slot; fence at the first end, perpendicular to the rail, with a downwardly projecting portion bearing on the workpiece edge, released by two screws in two corresponding holes and invertible so the projecting portion moves from one longitudinal side to the opposite side with the marked face still up; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing hole separation; two separate carriages each with an anti-rotation key in the slot, one cylindrical hardened-metal replaceable drill bushing with a vertical through bore registering with the slot, a threaded clamp knob whose shank passes through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, and its own pointer aligned with the bore axis and read against the distance marks so the reading difference is the center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index; the disclosed use sequence; the rigid-polymer-or-metal materials list; and the no-motor/battery/sensor/network negative limitation. Numeral usage is one-to-one and every numeral in the ledger appears in at least one figure brief, with no orphan numerals in any brief; parenthetical figure cross-references in the Detailed Description (14 in FIG. 4, 12 in FIG. 3, 16 and 18 in FIG. 2, 52/54/58/60 in FIG. 5, 72/74/78/80 in FIG. 3, 24/26/94 in FIG. 7, 34/36 in FIG. 6, 40 in FIG. 4) all match the briefs. Section lines are consistent: FIG. 2 carries designation 3 at both endpoints of the plane through the second guide carriage 70 and designation 5 at both endpoints of the plane through the first guide carriage 50, matching FIG. 3, FIG. 5, the Brief Description, and the Detailed Description. Claim and description terminology agree throughout (rail, fixed fence, downwardly projecting portion, guide carriage, key, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, transverse center index, sight notch, mounting holes), and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative remains. Schematic generic depictions (plain blocks for carriages, a plain round body for each knob in FIG. 1, plain rectangular fence bodies, the schematic slot outline) are confined to the figure briefs, are shape-neutral in the claims and description, and add no technical function, so I treated them as depiction conventions; the application text nowhere hedges an outline as shown "by way of example" or as "any closed outline." Two untraced substantive assertions remain and are reported: a figure-brief statement placing the marked centerline beyond the second end of the rail, and a Detailed Description assertion that pressing the fence squares the rail to the workpiece edge. Both convey functional geometry that no USER passage affirms, and each has a delete-only fix that leaves the filing clean.

findings.title: FIG. 7 brief locates the marked centerline beyond the second end of the rail, a positional relationship no inventor passage discloses and that conflicts with the transverse center index and the method step of moving the jig along the edge
findings.where: figures/FIG-7.md, centerline paragraph, final sentence (and the surrounding statement that the workpiece "remains visible ... beyond the second end of the rail 10")
findings.detail: The brief asserts where the workpiece centerline lies relative to the rail: "The centerline 94 appears on the workpiece 90 beyond the second end of the rail 10." Placing the pencil line off the far end of the rail conveys that the centerline runs lengthwise, colinear with the rail, rather than crossing it. That is a substantive geometric relationship, not page placement, and it is untraced. The disclosure says only that the index and notch are aligned with the line: "The user can align the center index and the sight notch with a pencil centerline on the workpiece before tightening both carriage knobs." It never says the centerline extends past the rail end or states the centerline's direction relative to the rail. The added placement also fights the rest of the candidate: the Detailed Description defines numeral 24 as "a mark that runs across the rail 10 transverse to the length of the rail 10," and claim 18 recites "moving the drilling jig along the straight edge until the transverse center index and the sight notch are aligned with the centerline," which only makes sense if the centerline crosses the rail transversely. The immediately preceding sentence of the same brief ("A centerline 94 is a single straight line drawn on the workpiece 90 and is aligned with the transverse center index 24 and with the sight notch 26") is source-faithful and should stay; only the added placement must go.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-7.md): "The centerline 94 appears on the workpiece 90 beyond the second end of the rail 10." Nearest inventor passage (input/disclosure.md): "A shallow V-shaped sight notch is formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the center index. The user can align the center index and the sight notch with a pencil centerline on the workpiece before tightening both carriage knobs." No affirmative passage states where the centerline lies relative to the rail's second end or in what direction it runs.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-7.md delete the sentence "The centerline 94 appears on the workpiece 90 beyond the second end of the rail 10." and delete the phrase "and beyond the second end of the rail 10" from the sentence "The workpiece 90 remains visible along both long sides of the band and beyond the second end of the rail 10.", leaving "The workpiece 90 remains visible along both long sides of the band." Retain the preceding sentence "A centerline 94 is a single straight line drawn on the workpiece 90 and is aligned with the transverse center index 24 and with the sight notch 26." No other text changes; the numeral list for FIG. 7 is unaffected.

findings.title: Detailed Description asserts that pressing the fence against the workpiece edge "squares the rail" to that edge, a function the inventor never attributes to the fence
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, method paragraph beginning "The user marks a centerline 94 on the front face of the workpiece 90"
findings.detail: The candidate states: "The downwardly projecting portion 32 of the fence 30, or the outer face of the spacer plate 40 when the spacer plate 40 is fitted, is pressed against the selected workpiece edge 92, which squares the rail 10 to that edge and fixes the setback." The setback half is supported; the squaring half is not. The disclosure assigns the fence exactly one control function: "The fence controls setback from the workpiece edge, while the two pointer readings control hole separation and the position of the pair relative to the centerline." The nearest passage about orientation is "The fence is perpendicular to the rail, so the rail extends inward across the workpiece when the fence bears against the edge," which states the rail's direction of extension, not that the fence trues or squares the rail to the edge. The added assertion is also in tension with the geometry the figure briefs depict, in which the rail lies spaced inward from and alongside the workpiece edge and only the projecting portion 32 touches that edge (FIG. 1: "A long straight rail 10 rests on the front face of the workpiece 90, spaced inward from the workpiece edge 92 ... The fence 30 has a downwardly projecting portion 32 that stands on the longitudinal side of the rail 10 that faces the workpiece edge 92 ... and contacts the workpiece edge 92."). Because this is a result attributed to a functional bearing face, it must be traced or removed.
findings.evidence: Candidate (draft/08-detailed-description.md): "... is pressed against the selected workpiece edge 92, which squares the rail 10 to that edge and fixes the setback." Inventor source (input/disclosure.md): "The fence controls setback from the workpiece edge, while the two pointer readings control hole separation and the position of the pair relative to the centerline." No affirmative passage says the fence squares, trues, or aligns the rail to the edge.
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md replace "which squares the rail 10 to that edge and fixes the setback" with "which fixes the setback", so the sentence reads: "The downwardly projecting portion 32 of the fence 30, or the outer face of the spacer plate 40 when the spacer plate 40 is fitted, is pressed against the selected workpiece edge 92, which fixes the setback." No claim, abstract, or figure-brief change is required; no claim recites squaring.
